newsitem.title: USA: ITT Hartford seen building reinsurance arm.
newsitem.headline: ITT Hartford seen building reinsurance arm.

text.p: ITT Hartford Group Inc 's agreement to buy the renewal rights of Security Re Companies reflects The Hartford's commitment to beefing up its reinsurance business, analysts said on Thursday.
Security Re is the reinsurance unit of New York-based Orion Capital Corp. Financial terms of the acquisition, announced earlier on Thursday, were not revealed.
"It makes both companies better off," said Gary Ransom, an analyst at Conning & Co. in Hartford. "It purifies what Orion is doing, and it helps build up one of The Hartford's important segments."

The deal was not a surprise, said Ransom. "Security Re was an operation that didn't completely fit with Orion. It was a small reinsurance company - and the market isn't going the way of the small reinsurance company, it's going the way of the large reinsurance company."
The Hartford's reinsurance arm, Hartford Re Co., is the nation's 11th-biggest reinsurer. It generated $522 million in net written premium last year.
The agreement to buy Security Re's renewal rights comes less than two weeks after The Hartford wrapped up the purchase of San Francisco Re's renewal rights.
Through both deals, Hartford Re Co. expects to assume more than $150 million of additional annual reinsurance premium, The Hartford said in a statement on Thursday.
Reinsurance should represent about 10 percent of The Hartford's projected $5.8 billion in property and casualty operations in calendar 1996, said Ransom.
One Wall Street analyst said that the Security Re deal was "positive to neutral" for The Hartford. He emphasized that The Hartford was buying only the renewal rights, not the company.
"It is just The Hartford reinforcing the fact that they are determined to grow their reinsurance business."
ITT Hartford Group's shares closed at 66-5/8, off 1/8 on Thursday, while Orion Capital's shares closed at 61-1/2 unchanged for the day on Thursday.
